A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AdaJudge and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. The method, experiments, and appendix material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations on RM-Bench and JudgeBench, component ablations in Tables 2-3, and representation and routing analyses in Figures 3-4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, revises the Phi-3.5 results, and adds training-resource measurements in Table 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same depth-gated representation refinement, three pooling perspectives, prompt-conditioned routing, and focal Bradley-Terry objective. Equations (1)-(6) are unchanged; the revised learning rate is an experimental-setting change.

E1.justification: Both versions train on HelpSteer3 preferences and evaluate on the same RM-Bench and JudgeBench domains and scenarios. Appendix C is unchanged. The added resource analysis introduces no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain the same four external reward models, controlled pooling baselines, and pooling/refinement ablations. Table 4 reports costs for existing pooling and component-removal variants rather than introducing a new comparison method. Newly cited routing methods are not evaluated as competitors.

E3.justification: Appendix A changes the reported Phi-3.5 learning rate from 4e-5 to 2e-5. Table 4 adds a resource-evaluation protocol reporting throughput, memory, and training time on the specified GPU. The accuracy metrics, benchmark protocols, backbone sizes, and other stated training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 4 examines computational overhead across all three backbones, comparing full AdaJudge with fixed pooling and Stage-I-only/Stage-II-only configurations. This adds evidence about component costs. The accuracy ablations and representation/routing analyses in Tables 2-3 and Figures 3-4 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for its experiments. The added resource table also presents point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises the Phi-3.5 results. RM-Bench overall scores for last-token/mean/AdaJudge change from 34.4/59.9/61.5 to 58.0/54.7/59.8; JudgeBench scores change from 43.1/53.1/57.4 to 55.1/55.7/59.4. This removes the earlier collapsed-baseline finding and reverses the static-pooling ranking on RM-Bench. These are revised-setting results, since the reported learning rate changes. Table 4 adds resource outcomes; Qwen results, external-baseline scores, and existing ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, pooling definitions, routing equations, and loss remain unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs. Adding the Bradley-Terry citation does not alter the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, central two-stage adaptation contribution, benchmark-superiority claims, and conclusion retain their meaning and scope. The introduction's shift from task-dependent to spatially diverse evidence refines the framing without introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the Phi representation-collapse/stability narrative with explanations involving capacity limits and gradient conflicts, and emphasizes parameter efficiency, avoidance of catastrophic forgetting, and a 'true Pareto improvement.' These materially revise the interpretation without adding corresponding mechanism tests. The limitations newly acknowledge text-only evaluation, and Appendix A adds an explanation of routing-related computational overhead.

D1.justification: Appendix A updates the Phi learning rate and replaces approximate training times of 6/6/8 hours with detailed resource reporting, including AdaJudge times of 7.71/8.08/10.80 hours for Phi-3.5/Qwen3-4B/Qwen3-8B. Table 4 supplies comparative memory and throughput figures. Hardware, remaining implementation details, and access information are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of judge deferral and model routing, citing Xu, Lu, and Wu and Lu, plus token/adaptive-pooling work by Ennadir, Brothers, and Wang. Additional citations support Bradley-Terry modeling and multimodal future work. These broaden the context while retaining the existing positioning around internal pooling experts versus multi-model ensembles.

P1.justification: The motivation paragraph, both related-work paragraphs, and all three main-results discussion blocks undergo substantial rewriting, with revised discussion headings and explanatory emphasis. Author affiliations and contact text also change. This is extensive prose revision despite retention of the overall section order and method exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds the resource-comparison Table 4 and corrects Figure 1's safety-example labels: last-token pooling changes from low to high score, and mean pooling from high to low. Its caption is rewritten around spatial evidence. The remaining figures and table structures are retained, with limited page reflow.

improvement.justification: Table 4 makes the computational trade-off assessable beyond v1's rough runtime estimates, Figure 1's contradictory labels are corrected, and text-only applicability is explicitly acknowledged. These provide a limited net improvement in transparency and clarity. However, the rewritten discussion overreaches: its new Pareto-improvement claim needs qualification because Table 1 reports Qwen3-8B Hard accuracy of 43.0 for AdaJudge versus 43.6 for mean pooling, and no dedicated experiment establishes avoidance of catastrophic forgetting.
